Good website design Corpus Christi companies can use starts with knowing who checks your site before they call. For a welding crew, an industrial cleaning outfit, a scaffold or equipment rental company or a safety trainer, that person is often a buyer or a superintendent at a plant along the ship channel. They are not shopping for a pretty home page. They want to know what you do, how you keep people safe, and whether you can be on site in Robstown or Ingleside by Monday.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan who writes and builds every site by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. You see a free demo of your site before you pay, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

A port city where the buyer is often a plant

The Port of Corpus Christi is the leading crude oil export port in the United States, and its chief executive has said roughly 60% of the crude the country exports leaves through it, about 2.3 million barrels a day. In 2025 the Corpus Christi Ship Channel handled 203.4 million tons of cargo, down 1.5% from the year before as crude eased and liquefied natural gas kept climbing. Refineries and plants sit along that channel, and Texas A&M's real estate research center counts nearly $60 billion of private investment in petrochemical and manufacturing sites near the port from 2012 to 2023.

The water shapes daily traffic too. The new Harbor Bridge, which opened in late June 2025 after nearly a decade of work, was built higher over the channel so bigger ships can reach the port, and TxDOT describes it as the longest concrete segmental cable-stayed bridge in North America. For a small contractor, all of this adds up to steady demand from big sites that are careful about whom they let through the gate.

What a plant buyer looks for on a contractor's site

Federal rules push large facilities to be choosy. Under OSHA's process safety management standard, an employer that brings in contractors for work in covered processes has to obtain and evaluate information about each contract employer's safety performance and programs when choosing one, and periodically evaluate their performance afterward. Paperwork and prequalification handle the formal part. Your website is often the first look, so it should answer the obvious questions before anyone has to ask:

  • Your crafts and services, in their words. Pipe welding, structural fabrication, hydro blasting, insulation, scaffolding, crane and lift rental, confined space training. Name each one you do and stop there.
  • Your safety program in plain English. What training your crews carry, how you run job safety briefings, who your safety contact is. Only list what you can back up with documents.
  • Equipment and crew size. A short, true list helps a superintendent judge whether you fit a turnaround or a small repair job.
  • Where you will work. Corpus Christi, Portland, Ingleside, Robstown, Aransas Pass, or further up the coast. Say it outright.
  • A downloadable capability statement. One page a buyer can forward to a manager, with the same facts as the site.
  • A name and a number. The person who quotes, and how to reach someone when a unit goes down at 2 a.m.

Notice what is not on that list: big claims. A buyer who has read a hundred vendor sites trusts specifics far more than adjectives, and we write that way on purpose.

Web design in Corpus Christi for each side of the bay

Not every Corpus Christi business sells to a refinery. The city is spread out along the water, and a home service company, a clinic or a shop reaches very different customers depending on the part of town.

AreaWho is searchingWhat the page should make clear
Downtown, the bayfront and Ocean DriveNeighbors along the water, office workers, visitorsParking, hours, and for trades, experience with older homes and salt air
The SouthsideFamilies in the newer subdivisionsFast booking, service on newer construction, reviews shown on the site
CalallenHouseholds on the northwest edge of the cityWhether you come out to them, and any trip charge stated up front
Flour BluffNeighbors near Naval Air Station Corpus Christi, Navy families among themPlain basics for people new to town: what you do, how to reach you, how fast
Portland, across the bayCommuters on US 181 over the Harbor BridgeThat you serve San Patricio County too, if you do
North Padre, Mustang Island, Port AransasIsland residents and first-time visitorsWhich island, how to get there, hours, booking

Google says local results weigh relevance, distance and prominence. Distance is fixed by where you are and where the searcher is, so the part you control is making it obvious which places you serve and what you do there.

The island trade, briefly

East of the city, Padre Island National Seashore protects what the National Park Service calls the largest stretch of undeveloped barrier island in the United States. Port Aransas, on the north end of Mustang Island, promotes the island's 18 miles of public beach, and a free TxDOT ferry links it to the mainland at Aransas Pass. Businesses out there sell to people who arrived an hour ago and are planning on a phone in a parking lot. A charter captain, a bait shop or a beach rental needs a site that loads fast on a weak signal, shows the meeting spot on a map and takes a booking request in a few taps. Everything else can wait further down the page.

A made-up example: a small fabrication shop in Calallen

Picture a six-person shop off the highway that does structural steel and pipe spools. Today its online presence is a map listing and a cousin's old site with a dead contact form. Work comes by word of mouth, and the owner loses bids to bigger outfits because a new buyer cannot find anything to forward upstairs.

The site we would write for a shop like that is short and specific: a home page that says what they fabricate and for whom, a services page per craft, a safety page in the owner's own words, a page about the area they cover, and a contact page with a quote form that goes straight to the estimator's inbox. Starter covers those five pages. If the shop wants pages for Portland, Ingleside and Robstown, each written about that town, Pro is the better fit. This example is invented to show the thinking; it is not a client.

Free business help across the Coastal Bend

  • Del Mar College Small Business Development Center. Funded in part by the SBA, the State of Texas, the City of Corpus Christi and the college, it offers no-cost one-on-one business advising, and its workshops are free or carry a small fee.
  • Coastal Bend Business Innovation Center at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. An EDA university center with an incubation program and consultation for growing companies.
  • United Corpus Christi Chamber of Commerce. Formed in 2015 when the memberships of the Corpus Christi Chamber and the Corpus Christi Hispanic Chamber agreed to merge. It has teamed up with the city on free seminars during National Small Business Week.

None of these build websites, and none send us work. They are simply worth a call before you spend money on anything, including us.

Common questions

What does website design in Corpus Christi cost?

It depends on who builds it and how the bill is set up. Some firms quote after a discovery meeting, some charge by the hour and some rent you a site by the month. We print ours: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each paid once. Hosting, maintenance and updates run $49 a month, and that charge goes away while you keep one of our AI agents. You see a free demo before you pay anything.

Will a website get my company on a refinery's approved vendor list?

No, and anyone who says it will is overselling. Plants and their contractor management systems run their own prequalification, with their own forms, insurance checks and safety reviews. A good site helps around that process: it shows the buyer who you are, what crafts and equipment you bring, your safety program in plain words, and how to reach the person who quotes. It makes the first conversation easier. It does not replace the paperwork.

Can one site cover Corpus Christi, Portland and Ingleside?

Yes, if you really work in all three. The honest way is a short section or page for each place you serve, saying what you do there and how fast you can get there, instead of a list of town names pasted into the footer. Our Pro package includes ten city pages, each researched and written from scratch, which suits a contractor who works both sides of the bay.

Is web design in Corpus Christi, TX different for island businesses?

The building blocks are the same, but the order changes. A charter, rental or cafe on Padre or Mustang Island gets many first-time visitors who do not know the area, so the site has to say plainly which island you are on, how to get there, your hours and how to book. A mainland contractor puts crafts, safety and coverage area first instead.

Who will I actually talk to?

Maurice Johnson, the person who writes and builds the site. Call (903) 636-7511 at any hour: an AI receptionist answers and transfers you to Maurice when you ask about a website preview or ask for him. You can also email maurice@dominionwebdesignpro.com.
